scope: Eight joining architectural sections for the requested monumental central citadel
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: one transparent modular architectural atlas for a distant illustrated fantasy map.
Create exactly EIGHT COMPLETE ISOLATED COMPONENTS in a 4-column by 2-row sheet, generous transparent gutters, no labels or grid. These components will stack and join in code into ONE monumental tiered capital citadel. Do NOT paint the complete citadel or an entire region in one cell. There is no landscape backdrop, map polygon, sky, scenic mountain painting, rectangular ground plate or city surrounding any component.

Design goal: a huge, unmistakable central fortress with a terraced, ascending silhouette, the fantasy archetype of Minas Tirith's layered citadel hierarchy, but an ORIGINAL severe Warlord design. It must dominate a surrounding city of tiny normal houses through the amount and height of its connected architecture. Do NOT enlarge the ordinary houses, doors or windows. Show many small window/buttress rhythms in broad wall masses: architectural scale, not a toy castle with a gigantic entrance. Use the FIRST reference only for the enemy identity and materials: inhabited armoured god-architecture, three rigid spear-like stone prongs bound by oxidized teal bands; vermilion and brick-red roofs and ceremonial cloth, muted slate/charcoal masonry, ossified rib/spine braces structurally holding walls and terraces. No generic skulls or tentacle decorations. Use the SECOND reference only for the map camera and surface treatment: distant three-quarter overhead from the south, clear roofs, upper-left light, deliberate hard pixel clusters, restrained hatching and selective dithering. Do not copy its standalone tiny-building compositions. This atlas needs broad building SECTIONS that form a SINGLE PALATIAL COMPLEX.

Exact row-major components:
1. Lower central front gate terrace: a broad gently convex retaining wall, a modest usable gateway and tiny red lintel banner, stepped upper parapet and upper-level access. This is the base-middle architectural section, not a whole castle.
2. Matching LOWER LEFT curved terrace wing: a sweeping curved rib-braced grey stone wall with low red-roof galleries on its top, exposed inner end designed to overlap the central gate section, slightly broken outer edge. Left half only.
3. Matching LOWER RIGHT curved terrace wing: complementary right half, same floor level, masonry rhythm and top galleries. Right half only.
4. Rear terraced buttress section: an irregular low mass of several connected stone retaining piers and ossified structural ribs, useful as the back support behind the other levels, with no scenic rock mountain or ground tile.
5. Middle elevated terrace collar: one broad shallow U-shaped arc of fortification with a red-roof gallery along its rear and quiet interior court; transparent outside, roofline at the level that can sit behind the lower gate terrace. Not a complete city ring and not a freestanding toy castle.
6. Upper palace body: a vertical severe rectangular great hall and attached narrow wings, small normal-size windows, red roof planes and teal binding bands; a coherent simple silhouette with one understated entrance. The summit will be a separate component.
7. Summit crown section: three tall, narrow, rigid spear-prong stone towers bound across their lower third by ONE heavy teal bridge-band, the central prong taller. Their lower palace-roof joining surface is visible, but no lower terraces, complete fortress or city is included. Dark red vertical insets, tiny windows; not a pasted crest.
8. Broken outer stepped rampart section: a short curved low imperial wall and stair/terrace edge with partial red roofing and restrained rib-built supports, matching the lower terraces and usable at their fringe.

The joining interfaces are construction ends, no scenic cut edges. Every component remains whole, centred with generous true-alpha margins, including every tall spire. No part touches another cell. All eight share the SAME tiny door/window/stone scale and camera. Parts 1-5 spread through more material and many tiny masonry bays; do not give them oversized individual doorways. The silhouette and large calm middle-value planes must read after reduction to map size. Dark fantasy, austere and oppressive, inhabited rather than abandoned. Decay remains secondary: repaired inner masonry, more broken outer works. Broad material value groups, no all-black mass, no glittering cream outlines everywhere, no golden magical light. All colour is in actual local materials. No people, discernible faces, skull faces, eyes, wounds or gore. No writing, UI, frames, vignettes or faction icon overlays. Preserve the existing surrounding houses' scale. True transparent background.
